intro.text:
The tables below define the display, labelling, and behavioural requirements for the Bank Data Sharing
 consents in the TPP Consent Management Interface (CMI). See the User Experience
 page for interactive wireframes of the dashboard and detail pages.

Adjustments to the requirements below are permitted provided the customer can always clearly understand what consents they have granted. Any adjustments must be documented in your CX certification submission.

blocks.text: The dashboard must present Bank Data Sharing consents across two tabs.

rows:
The Current
 tab must display all consents whose status is AwaitingAuthorization
, Authorized
, Suspended
, or Paused
.

The History
 tab must display all consents whose status is Rejected
, Expired
, or Revoked
.

blocks.text: A filter panel must be available on the dashboard. The following three filters are required:

rows: Dynamically populated from the LFIs present in the user's connections
Dynamically populated from the types present in the current tab
Dynamically populated from the statuses present in the current tab

blocks.text: Consent statuses must be translated from their API values into user-friendly labels before display.
Each Bank Data Sharing consent card on the dashboard must show the following fields.

rows: Name of the LFI the consent is held with

Number of connected accounts, e.g. 1 Account Connected
 or 2 Accounts Connected
Date the most recent data was retrieved under this consent

blocks.text:
Selecting a consent on the dashboard opens its detail page. The detail page presents the same information the customer saw on the Consent Page at the time they gave consent — the permissions, accounts, and conditions that defined what they agreed to. This gives the customer a clear reference point for what they originally authorised, without requiring them to recall it from memory. In addition to all fields shown on the dashboard card, the detail page must show a truncated Consent ID with a copy button (format: f47ac10b...d479
).

rows: List of all accounts the user has connected under this consent, each showing account type name and full IBAN

Expandable list of data categories the consent covers, derived from the consent's Permissions
 field

sections.heading: Detail page > Detail page — List of Updates

blocks.text:
When a consent carries a BaseConsentId
, a List of Updates
 link must be shown on the detail page. Clicking this link navigates to a dedicated view that displays all consents related to the current consent through the same BaseConsentId
. The related consents are retrieved via GET /account-access-consents
, passing the baseConsentId
 query parameter. A consent is included in the list if: its BaseConsentId
 matches the current consent's BaseConsentId
, or

its ConsentId
 matches the current consent's BaseConsentId


 The current consent must not
 appear in its own list of updates.

sections.heading: Detail page > Detail page — List of Updates > Each related consent card

blocks.text: Each related consent must be displayed in the same visual format as the dashboard connection list, with the following differences:

rows: Date the consent was last updated
Type label from Consent type labels
Date the most recent data was retrieved

blocks.text: Each card must include a chevron and hover interaction matching the dashboard, and clicking a card must navigate to the detail page for that consent. No status badge is shown on the update cards.

blocks.text:
No action buttons are shown when status is Expired
, Rejected
, or Revoked
.

When the user selects Pause, Reactivate, or Revoke, replace the detail view with a single confirmation screen
 that includes: a title, a description of the impact of the action on the service, a Confirm button, and a Go back button.

Once a user confirms the action, the change must take effect immediately — there must be no delay between confirmation and the consent reflecting its new state. Revoke
 Immediate PATCH to /account-access-consents/{ConsentId}

Pause
 No API Hub update — record paused state in the TPP's own system only
Reactivate
 No API Hub update — clear the paused state in the TPP's own system only
